correctness_confidence.basis: The classical mathematical chain (Haar measure on S^3, Chebyshev orbital integrals, character convolution, heat-kernel semigroup, 3-spoke gauge fixing, and reduced-schedule elimination) is mathematically sound. However, the Lean code was not supplied or executed in this review run, and the arbitrary-cellulation original-edge claim in the historical abstract is explicitly unproved in this version.

novelty.basis: As the author candidly notes, the analytic and combinatorial identities for 2D SU(2) Yang-Mills are classical (Migdal, Witten, Driver). The contribution lies in their concrete Lean 4/Mathlib formalization, including all-order Chebyshev orbital integration, infinite heat-kernel convolution via dominated convergence, and certified graph-elimination schedules.

reproducibility.basis: The manuscript specifies exact Lean declaration names and a pinned GitHub commit hash (c13451842768e02a3c97afe11c8dcb9523c2c727). However, no source archive was included in the review packet and this assessment had no execution or browsing tools to independently compile the Lean project, verify Mathlib versions, or confirm axiom-free compilation.

rigor.basis: The mathematical arguments presented in the text carefully address convergence (dominated convergence for infinite character sums), endpoint singularities in Chebyshev integrals, and explicit measure-preserving maps. Nonetheless, a mismatch exists between the historical abstract/title and the proved scope (which stops at the post-gauge-fixed schedule evaluator for general cyclic duals), rectified only via a prepended supersession notice.

significance.basis: Formalizing compact Lie group harmonic analysis (SU(2) orbital integrals, character convolution, and heat-kernel semigroups) and lattice gauge reductions in Lean 4/Mathlib is a useful contribution to mechanized mathematical physics, though restricted here to 2D SU(2) reduced schedules and partial gauge-fixing.

potential_errors: In the historical manuscript body (page 3), the title and abstract state the exact simple-loop area law for finite oriented disk cellulations without qualification, whereas pages 8, 9, and 11 clarify that for general cellulations with dual cycles, the theorem applies to the post-gauge-fixed recursive schedule amplitude rather than the unreduced original-edge product-Haar integral.

The artifact bundles a two-page 'Version 2 - supersession and correction note' atop the unchanged nine-page historical 'version 1' manuscript, creating an internal structural inconsistency where the front matter retracts the authority of the body's title and abstract and defers the complete proof to an external document (ai.viXra:2607.0039v1).
strengths: Transparent and detailed claim boundary declarations, both in the prepended correction notice (pages 1-2) and in Sections 6.2, 7, and 10 of the main text, clearly distinguishing proved reduced-schedule statements from unproved arbitrary-cellulation edge reductions.

Clean analytical pipeline from the S^3 Haar probability measure and first-rail squared-mass moments (u = |a|^2 uniform on [0,1]) to all-order SU(2) Chebyshev orbital integrals without singular sine-division issues at the endpoints x = +/-1.
Rigorous treatment of the infinite heat-kernel convolution K_s * K_t = K_{s+t} for s, t > 0 via finite partial sums and dominated convergence using uniform Casimir majorants.

Explicit measure-preserving gauge-fixing transformations constructed for the cyclic 3-spoke disk (K_3 dual), arbitrary finite-valence star graphs, and global vertex-tree coordinates on finite connected simple graphs.
strong_novelty_candidates: End-to-end Lean 4/Mathlib formalization of the SU(2) heat-kernel semigroup identity and translated character convolution directly from spherical Haar measure and Chebyshev orbital integration.
Mechanized construction of certified face-elimination schedules on finite connected dual graphs paired with schedule-independence proofs for the recursive Migdal amplitude.
summary: This artifact presents a Lean 4/Mathlib formalization of exact two-dimensional SU(2) Yang-Mills theory in the heat-kernel formulation, covering the identification of normalized Haar measure on SU(2) with S^3, all-order Chebyshev orbital integration, translated character convolution, the infinite heat-kernel semigroup K_s * K_t = K_{s+t}, two-face Migdal subdivision, explicit product-Haar gauge fixing for the three-spoke cyclic lattice and vertex trees, and schedule-independent face elimination for finite connected disk cellulations. Notably, the PDF prepends a two-page supersession and correction notice onto the nine-page historical manuscript. Both the notice and pages 8, 9, and 11 of the body acknowledge that for general cellulations with dual cycles, this version proves the area law only for the post-gauge-fixed recursive schedule evaluator and vertex-tree coordinates, leaving open the edge-space decomposition SU(2)^E ~= SU(2)^{V\{r}} x SU(2)^{E\T} and simultaneous facial-holonomy transport (which are deferred to a separate successor paper, ai.viXra:2607.0039v1). Because the Lean source archive was not provided in this review packet and no execution tools are available, formal compilation could not be independently verified; static inspection confirms the classical mathematics is sound within the narrowed scope.
unresolved_material_objections: Incomplete closure of the arbitrary-cellulation original-edge physical integral within this manuscript: as acknowledged on pages 1-2 and 8-11, this version does not prove the edge-space product-Haar decomposition SU(2)^E ~= SU(2)^{V\{r}} x SU(2)^{E\T} or simultaneous facial-holonomy transport for general cellulations with dual cycles, so the main simple-loop area law stated in the body's title and abstract is established only for the post-gauge-fixed schedule evaluator (and the K_3 three-spoke case) unless supplemented by the external successor paper.
weaknesses: The manuscript relies on a prepended correction notice pointing to an external successor preprint (ai.viXra:2607.0039v1) rather than either revising the internal title/abstract of the body or incorporating the complete tree-cotree original-edge proof directly into a self-contained paper.

The exposition of the Lean formalization is predominantly a high-level summary of declaration names and classical mathematical formulas, providing very few actual type signatures or formal definitions (e.g., the exact Lean structure definition of SU2FiniteDiskCellulation is described only in prose).
No source code archive was included in the review packet, preventing static or executable verification of the Lean definitions and theorem statements beyond the prose descriptions in the PDF.
